clue.text: Low criminal very slow trailing detectives

indicators.note: trailing means the rest of the pieces come behind the detectives, so they are placed after them

parts.note: DIS are Detective Inspectors, plural of DI
a con is a convict, a criminal
so means very, as in 'so tired'
late means behind time, slow to arrive

explanation.surface: A lowlife crook dawdles along behind the police officers on his case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailing' says the detectives come first in the answer although they are last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low is being downcast and miserable, which is what a heartbroken, inconsolable person is.

clue.text: Be virtuous about starting to water shrub

indicators.note: about means the phrase for being virtuous goes round the other piece

parts.note: to do good is to behave virtuously

indicators.note: starting to points to the opening letter of the word water

explanation.surface: A gardening tip: be good and remember to start watering your bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts W, the first letter of 'water', inside DO GOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornus, the plant genus with red winter stems, is a flowering bush grown widely in gardens.

clue.text: Stick typifying authority for faithful initially …

definitions.text: Stick typifying authority for faithful initially

indicators.note: initially says to take the opening letter of each of the preceding words in turn

explanation.surface: A rod held as a symbol of power over the faithful, like a bishop's crook.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a crosier or rod of office, and its first five words begin S, T, A, F, F.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod carried as an emblem of office, like a crosier for a bishop's flock, is the classic symbol of authority.

clue.text: … old organised church holds sound sacrament

indicators.note: holds means the word for organised contains the noise word within it

parts.note: ran, as in ran the show, means organised
a din is a loud sound
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An ancient, well-run church keeps up a valid sacramental rite.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the one before only for the surface reading; 'organised' is a synonym here, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In many Protestant churches a rite such as baptism or communion is called an ordinance rather than a sacrament.

clue.text: Reportedly get away to Oxford?

indicators.note: reportedly says a word that is heard, not written, is meant

parts.note: shoo! is the cry telling an animal to get away

explanation.surface: Is someone being told to clear off to the university town?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' seems to be the city or university; it is a style of laced leather footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a classic lace-up leather brogue-style item of footwear, so the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Subject of fiction with grand elevated title

parts.note: a lie is a fiction, an untruth
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: elevated in a down clue means the word for title is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a name is a title

explanation.surface: The subject of a novel turns out to be someone given a lofty title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns NAME into EMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal vassal owing loyalty to a lord was that lord's subject, sworn to serve him.

clue.text: Raising small change gives rises in liquidity?

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the pieces are written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: to edit something is to change it

explanation.surface: Putting up the small change brings an increase in a firm's cash flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' turns SEDIT into TIDES. 'liquidity' looks like finance; here it is just being liquid, like the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea level climbs and falls twice a day, so its regular swells are rises in a liquid body.

clue.text: Eager to capture one in nude perhaps

indicators.note: to capture means the word for eager surrounds the other piece

parts.note: panting for something is being eager for it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone keen to catch a naked figure, perhaps an art student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to capture' puts I inside PANTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A nude is one kind of artwork in oils or watercolour, so perhaps signals an example.

clue.text: Turn out with a French drink raised

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the drink word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a gulp is a swallow of drink

explanation.surface: A night out ends with a French drink being lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns GULP into PLUG.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn out a light or appliance is to switch it off, as pulling its plug from the socket does.

clue.text: Bash organised for pretentious

indicators.note: to bash something is to batter it out of shape, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A party that has been well organised can seem showy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' looks like a party noun; it is the anagram signal working on 'organised'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something showy and overblown, aiming to impress, is pompous or pretentious.

clue.text: Beginning to trap Queen with no winner

indicators.note: to trap means the word for beginning encloses the other piece

parts.note: the dawn of something is its beginning
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A chess opening that traps the queen ends with nobody winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to trap' puts R inside DAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A match that is tied, ending level with neither side victorious, is a draw.

clue.text: Rotten tip giving insult

parts.note: food that is off has gone rotten
the end of something is its tip

explanation.surface: A lousy gratuity is an affront to the waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' suggests money left for a waiter; it is the end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To insult someone is to give them offence, hurting their feelings or affronting them.

clue.text: Some eavesdropper's on a line getting offensive

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A snoop listening in on a phone line turns abusive.
explanation.definitionFit: When remarks get personal they attack someone's character or looks, which is being rude and offensive.

clue.text: Treating villain admitting offence

indicators.note: admitting means the villain word lets the other piece in

parts.note: a dog is a contemptible scoundrel, a villain
a sin is an offence

explanation.surface: A medic is treating a criminal who confesses his wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' means confessing on the surface but letting in for the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor treating a patient gives measured amounts of medicine, the administration of doses.

clue.text: Setter's first clue finishes making allowances

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word Setter's

parts.note: a tip is a clue or hint
ends are finishes

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler earns his fees once the first clue is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed regular sum paid to clergy, students or trainees is a salary-like allowance.

clue.text: Worrying about empty table supplying food

indicators.note: about means the worrying word goes round the other piece

parts.note: caring, as in caring about something, means being concerned or worrying

indicators.note: empty means the inside of table is removed, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: Fretting over a bare table while laying on a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worrying' is read as caring about something, being concerned.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms that provide meals for weddings or events are in the business of serving dishes to guests.

clue.text: Dry lecture follows hoisting of flag

indicators.note: follows means the lecture word comes after the other piece
hoisting of in a down clue means the flag word is lifted, written upwards and so backwards

parts.note: to flag a path is to lay it with flagstones, to pave it
to orate is to lecture or speechify

explanation.surface: A tedious speech comes after the flag is run up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like an adjective describing the lecture; it is a verb. 'hoisting of' turns PAVE into EVAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that turns into vapour leaves a surface dry, so to dry up is to vaporise away.

clue.text: Track over information for virus?

parts.note: a path is a track
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Tracing a route with data to follow the spread of an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus is one example of a germ or agent causing disease, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Old and prudish, oddly enviable

parts.note: prim means prudish and proper

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Being old-fashioned and strait-laced is, strangely, something to envy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes E, V, A, L from 'enviable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Primeval things date from the earliest ages of the world, so they are ancient.

clue.text: Group is told to purchase weapon

indicators.note: purchase is a grip or hold, so the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A gang is instructed to buy a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like buying; it means a grip, the words holding the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a small handgun, a type of firearm.

clue.text: Group excursions after vacation in river

indicators.note: after means the outside letters come behind the group word

parts.note: a gang is a group

indicators.note: vacation means emptying the word excursions, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A party of tourists take holiday trips on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' sounds like a holiday; it means emptying 'excursions' to ES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ganges is the great sacred watercourse of northern India.

clue.text: Scoffed at opening of Spam, preserved

indicators.note: opening of points to the first letter of the word Spam

parts.note: corned beef is salted to preserve it

explanation.surface: Someone sneered at a tin of Spam once it was opened, finding it just salted meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff at someone is to mock them, to treat them with contempt and disdain.

clue.text: Sly bird, tense, having timid exterior

indicators.note: exterior means the timid word forms the outside, wrapping around the other pieces

parts.note: shy means timid
a teal is a small duck
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A cunning bird, tense and nervy on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is only a link here; 'exterior' alone signals the wrap-around.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sly is being furtive and secretive, moving quietly so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Range with new material

parts.note: a line is a range of products

explanation.surface: A fashion house's collection features a new fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is cloth woven from flax, a textile used for sheets and summer suits.

clue.text: City of the Spanish upset in agitation

indicators.note: in means the reversed article goes inside the word for agitation

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss, a state of agitation

indicators.note: upset means the Spanish article is turned over, written backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish city caught up in commotion and upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: A to-do is a commotion or fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic walled place in central Spain, famed for its swords; there is also one in Ohio.

clue.text: Live with former partner first …

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
first is abbreviated 1st, with the numeral 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Moving in with one's former partner before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the next for the surface only. '1st' must be read with the figure 1 as a letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be alive, to have being and continue living.

clue.text: … naughty sweetheart is desired

parts.note: bad means naughty
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A wicked lover is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover; it is the middle of the word 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bade is the past of bid, so it means asked, wished or ordered someone to do something.

clue.text: Past is glorious first off

indicators.note: first off means the first letter of the glorious word is removed

parts.note: a golden age is a glorious one

explanation.surface: Nostalgia: the past was glorious, to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an old-fashioned adjective meaning bygone or of former times, as in the olden days.

clue.text: Trod again, changing step

indicators.note: changing means the letters of the two words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Walking the same route once more, but changing one's stride.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradation is one stage in a series of gradual changes, a degree on a scale.

clue.text: Apathetic teen intrudes furiously

indicators.note: furiously means the letters are thrown about wildly into a new order

explanation.surface: A listless adolescent barges in in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone apathetic shows no concern or enthusiasm, being bored and indifferent.
